newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy must say what comes after 'Euro-tax'-Draghi.
newsitem.headline: Italy must say what comes after 'Euro-tax'-Draghi.

text.p: The Italian government must explain shortly how it plans to replace the one-off 'Euro-tax' and keep the ratio between the budget deficit and GDP below three percent in 1998, Treasury Director General Mario Draghi said in a speech on Friday.

The government plans to raise 12.5 trillion lire ($8.4 billion) next year from the so-called Euro-tax in a bid to prepare the economy for the single European currency. It has promised to partially compensate tax-payers for the levy.
"In order that this tax does not have a recessionary impact, it has to be seen in a credible fashion as temporary," Draghi said in a speech to a conference in this central Italian city.

"The 1998 budget must therefore specify, before the economy reduces its spending scope, what other measures will be taken to hold the deficit/GDP below three percent without the 1997 Euro-tax," he added.
Opposition parties have lashed the Euro-tax, with former finance minister Giulio Tremonti saying he did not think it would be either temporary nor re-imbursed. ($1=1495 Lire)
